chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “None of you should urinate while his private part is exposed to the moon, facing it.”

Then he said: The least that suffices him for his purification from urine is that he wash the place of its خروج with water in an amount twice what is upon it of the urine; and in thoroughness of purification from it is whatever exceeds that amount.

key_terms.مَوْضِعَ خُرُوجِهِ: the place from which it exits

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about etiquette during urination and the minimum washing required for purification from urine?
ai.summary: This hadith gives an etiquette related to relieving oneself and also states a ruling concerning purification from urine. It combines bodily modesty with practical instruction on taharah, indicating both proper conduct and the minimum sufficient washing for cleanliness.
